description:
This iteration's mandated task was to independently re-derive, from scratch, the FULL (function, parameter) classification table for every pure function in the Purity Boundary Map -- not merely spot-check the iteration-17 builder's own table -- and compare for discrepancies. Doing so surfaces exactly one discrepancy, but it is a real, well-evidenced one: the builder's own table (reviews/spec/iteration-17/RESOLUTION-NOTES.md:140) classifies `decideColonySpawn`'s `colonySurplusUsd` parameter as DERIVED-BOUND, citing as its sole basis 'REQ-102 EARS clause: "WHEN REQ-101's colony surplus is computed" -- ties directly to `computeColonySurplusUsd`'. Independent re-verification shows this citation does NOT meet the evidentiary bar the SAME builder's own table applied one row earlier, and does not meet the bar REQ-102's own text applies to `colonySurplusUsd`'s two immediate signature-siblings in the exact same function.

The established pattern in this spec (used to resolve FIND-1401 for `recentSpawnAttempts`, FIND-1501 for `childrenProvisioning`, FIND-1601(a) for `deployTarget`, and this iteration's own preemptive fix for `filterProductiveCitizens`'s `ledgerRows`/`citizens`) is an explicit sentence of the exact shape 'X is never hand-assembled by the calling orchestration -- it is ALWAYS the direct return value of Y(...)', PLUS a dedicated proof obligation (PROP-102g, PROP-102i, PROP-202d, PROP-101j respectively) requiring both a Tier-1 control-flow read AND a Tier-2 integration test against real data. A grep of behavioral-spec.md for the phrase 'hand-assembled' (6 occurrences) shows it is used for `ledgerRows`(x2), `recentSpawnAttempts`, `childrenProvisioning`, `deployTarget`, and `initialSkills` -- never once for `colonySurplusUsd`. In REQ-102's own Acceptance Criteria list (behavioral-spec.md:920-939), the bullet at line 920 lists `decideColonySpawn`'s full signature including `colonySurplusUsd` as its very FIRST parameter; the very next two bullets (lines 929-933 and 934-939) give `recentSpawnAttempts` and `childrenProvisioning` -- `colonySurplusUsd`'s own immediate signature-siblings -- their own dedicated 'is never hand-assembled... ALWAYS the direct return value of `deriveRecentSpawnAttempts({ledgerRows: readChildren(...)})`/`countChildrenProvisioning({ledgerRows: readChildren(...)})`' bullets. `colonySurplusUsd` itself never receives an equivalent bullet anywhere in this Acceptance Criteria list, or anywhere else in either spec document.

The same asymmetry recurs in verification-architecture.md's own Purity Boundary Map row for `decideColonySpawn` (line 201): that single row explicitly documents the real-derivation binding for `recentSpawnAttempts` ('NEVER hand-assembled... always the direct return value of the new `deriveRecentSpawnAttempts`'), for `childrenProvisioning` ('likewise NEVER hand-assembled... always the direct return value of the new `countChildrenProvisioning`'), and even gives `spawnThresholdUsd` a full derivation formula ('itself computed upstream of this function's own call from `MIN_SHELTER_USD * SAFETY_MARGIN_MULTIPLIER`') -- but says nothing whatsoever about where `colonySurplusUsd`, the row's own first-listed parameter, comes from at REQ-102's real call site. The only two proof obligations that touch `colonySurplusUsd` at all, PROP-102a (line 372, 'colonySurplusUsd === spawnThresholdUsd exactly -> eligible:true') and PROP-102d (line 375, 'Non-finite/negative colonySurplusUsd input is treated as 0'), both treat it purely as an ALREADY-GIVEN fixture value for testing `decideColonySpawn`'s own internal boundary/fail-closed logic -- exactly the same category of test PROP-101d/PROP-101e were shown (by this SAME iteration-17 fix, at behavioral-spec.md:432 / verification-architecture.md's own FIND-1601 changelog paragraph) to be insufficient proxies for a real-orchestration binding proof. No PROP-102g/PROP-102i/PROP-202d/PROP-101j-equivalent obligation exists requiring a Tier-1 control-flow read (confirming REQ-102's real caller passes `computeColonySurplusUsd(...)`'s direct return value as `colonySurplusUsd`, never a hand-rolled/cached/stale figure) or a Tier-2 integration test (writing real registry/ledger data, calling the real pipeline `readCitizenBalances(filterProductiveCitizens(...))` -> `computeColonySurplusUsd(...)`, and asserting `decideColonySpawn`'s real orchestration is invoked with EXACTLY that value for THAT SAME evaluation).

This is not a cosmetic omission. `colonySurplusUsd` is the single most consequential value `decideColonySpawn` consumes -- it is the number that, gated only by the cooldown/concurrency checks, determines whether ANY spawn happens at all this wake. A hand-assembled or stale `colonySurplusUsd` is exactly the same class of concrete, deploy-relevant hazard FIND-1601(a) identified for `deployTarget`: REQ-102's own edge case (behavioral-spec.md:898-902) already contemplates 'Two or more spawn evaluations run in the same wake cycle... the gate function ITSELF is pure and may return eligible:true from both evaluations' -- but nothing in either spec states that each of those separate evaluations is required to call `computeColonySurplusUsd(...)` FRESH rather than reusing an earlier evaluation's (possibly stale, possibly hand-computed-differently) aggregate figure. An implementer could plausibly compute the colony surplus once per wake and pass the cached number into multiple `decideColonySpawn` calls, or -- worse -- reimplement a shortcut sum inline at the call site that skips `filterProductiveCitizens`'s exclusion logic (e.g. accidentally including a `"bootstrap_failed"` citizen's balance), and no proof obligation in this spec would catch either mistake.

Critically, this discrepancy demonstrates the structured classification methodology itself still has a blind spot in exactly the dimension this iteration's dispatch asked to test: the iteration-17 builder's own table applied the CORRECT, rigorous standard to `filterProductiveCitizens`'s `ledgerRows`/`citizens` one row earlier in the SAME table (row 133-134, explicitly rejecting a similarly weak conceptual tie-in and requiring the full 'never hand-assembled + dedicated PROP' treatment) -- yet accepted a strictly weaker form of the identical weak evidence (a generic EARS-clause phrase, with no 'never hand-assembled' sentence and no dedicated PROP) as sufficient for `colonySurplusUsd`, one row later, in the very same table. This is the SIXTH instance of this recurring failure class across iterations 14-18 (after `recentSpawnAttempts`, `childrenProvisioning`, `measured_last_shelter_cost_usd`, `deployTarget`+`initialSkills` (counted together as FIND-1601), and `filterProductiveCitizens`'s own `ledgerRows`/`citizens`) -- meaning the failure class has NOT genuinely converged this iteration, contrary to what a reading limited to 'the builder's table found nothing new' would conclude.

evidence.snippet: REQ-102's own EARS clause: 'WHEN REQ-101's colony surplus is computed, THE SYSTEM SHALL permit at most one new spawn attempt when, and only when, `colonySurplusUsd >= SPAWN_THRESHOLD_USD` AND the Cooldown Check below evaluates to "not on cooldown"...' -- this is generic scene-setting prose, not the explicit 'never hand-assembled, always the direct return value of X(...)' binding sentence this spec's own established discipline requires for a real, computed, cross-function-derived aggregate value

Acceptance Criteria: line 920 lists `decideColonySpawn`'s full signature with `colonySurplusUsd` as its first parameter; lines 929-933 and 934-939 give `colonySurplusUsd`'s own immediate signature-siblings, `recentSpawnAttempts` and `childrenProvisioning`, their own dedicated '(resolves FIND-1401)'/'(new, resolves FIND-1501)' bullets stating each 'is never hand-assembled by the calling orchestration -- it is ALWAYS the direct return value of' its respective named derivation function. No equivalent bullet exists anywhere for `colonySurplusUsd`

The Purity Boundary Map's own `decideColonySpawn` row explicitly documents the real-derivation binding for `recentSpawnAttempts` ('NEVER hand-assembled... always the direct return value of the new `deriveRecentSpawnAttempts`'), `childrenProvisioning` ('likewise NEVER hand-assembled... always the direct return value of the new `countChildrenProvisioning`'), and gives `spawnThresholdUsd` a full derivation formula -- but states nothing about `colonySurplusUsd`'s own real-system-state source anywhere in the same row

PROP-102a ('colonySurplusUsd === spawnThresholdUsd exactly -> eligible:true') and PROP-102d ('Non-finite/negative colonySurplusUsd input is treated as 0') are the only two proof obligations touching `colonySurplusUsd` -- both treat it as an already-given fixture value for `decideColonySpawn`'s own internal-logic tests; no PROP-102g/PROP-102i/PROP-202d/PROP-101j-equivalent real-derivation integration obligation exists for it

The iteration-17 builder's own independently-built classification table: rows 133-134 correctly reject a weak conceptual tie-in for `filterProductiveCitizens`'s `ledgerRows`/`citizens` ('No prior "never hand-assembled" phrase existed... now bound explicitly...') and require the full binding-sentence-plus-PROP treatment; row 140 accepts a strictly weaker, structurally identical form of evidence -- a single EARS-clause phrase with no 'never hand-assembled' sentence and no dedicated PROP -- as sufficient grounds for classifying `colonySurplusUsd` DERIVED-BOUND, one row later in the SAME table

REQ-102's own edge case: 'Two or more spawn evaluations run in the same wake cycle... the gate function ITSELF is pure and may return eligible:true from both evaluations' -- confirms multiple `decideColonySpawn` evaluations within one wake are an explicitly contemplated scenario, yet neither spec document ever requires each such evaluation to call `computeColonySurplusUsd(...)` fresh rather than reusing an earlier evaluation's aggregate figure
